screens.prompt: In B9, say missing when the code in A8 is not in the table, and found when it is.

hints.syntax: =IF(ISNA(test),"missing","found") — the IS function goes inside the IF test.
hints.func-if: Two words come out of the formula, so it needs an IF to choose between them.
hints.func-isna: A match that fails raises #N/A, and ISNA is the test that recognises exactly that error.
hints.require-ref: Search for the code in the grid rather than typing Q-9.
hints.value: Q-9 is not in the code column, so the match fails with #N/A and the answer is missing.
hints.error: ISNA is a test, so arithmetic on its result gives #VALUE! rather than a word.

a comparison to the code can only answer for that one value, not for a lookup that misses
the two words are the wrong way round, so a miss reads as found

screens.prompt: In B9, say out of range when the price column of the second column is not inside the table, otherwise fine.

hints.syntax: =IF(ISERROR(INDEX(A2:B7,1,3)),"out of range","fine") — the test wraps the whole call.
hints.func-if: The formula has to choose between two words, so an IF carries the test.
hints.func-iserror: Any error at all is what this question asks about, and that is ISERROR.
hints.require-ref: Point at the table itself rather than typing the range by hand.
hints.value: The table has two columns, so asking for a third raises #REF! and the answer is out of range.
hints.error: Dividing the word out of range by zero replaces it with #VALUE!.

reject.why: a #REF! is not #N/A, so the narrower test answers fine
the second column exists, so nothing fails and the answer is fine
the two words are the wrong way round, so a real #REF! reads as fine
the test alone returns true or false, and the question asks for a word
a different range is tested, so the grid's table is never read
the text answer is then divided by zero
the IF is missing its opening parenthesis

docs.explain: An error in Excel is a value, not a crash: #N/A, #REF!, #VALUE!, #DIV/0!, #NAME? and #NUM! each sit in a cell and can be tested like anything else. Three tests matter here. ISNA answers TRUE only for #N/A, the error a lookup or a match raises when nothing matched, which is usually a data question rather than a formula question. ISERROR answers TRUE for any error at all, which is what you want when the question is simply whether the calculation worked. ISERR is the same test minus #N/A, for the rarer case where a missing match is expected and any other error is not. Reading the difference matters because the three errors come from three different problems: #N/A is a value that is not in the list, #REF! is a reference that no longer points at anything, and #VALUE! is the wrong kind of value in an arithmetic operation. In this drill the code Q-9 is missing, so ISNA says TRUE and the formula prints missing; the second screen asks the table for a third column, which raises #REF!, and ISERROR turns that into the words out of range. Both screens leave the error visible in the logic rather than deleting it.
